instantiated_cells.justification: The only periodic spending/expense statement required by the statute is a principal’s expense statement due July 31 and January 31, not an annual lobbyist-filed spending report.
The statute requires semiannual filing by principals on July 31 and January 31 and contains no monthly lobbyist spending report requirement.
Periodic spending disclosure is assigned to principals (with lobbyists only supplying information), so there is no separate lobbyist spending report on any other cadence.
Expense statements are filed semiannually by principals and the statute does not establish a quarterly lobbyist spending report.
Wisconsin requires the principal (not the lobbyist) to file the periodic expense statement, so there is no separate semiannual lobbyist spending report with the lobbyist as named filer.
The statute sets fixed semiannual deadlines (July 31 and January 31) for principal filings and contains no triannual/legislative-calendar lobbyist spending report.
Itemized spending disclosures are required in the principal’s expense statement, while lobbyists merely provide information to the principal and do not file a separate itemized spending report.
The statute imposes periodic expense-statement filing obligations on registered principals and only requires lobbyists to provide information to principals, not to file separate spending reports.
Disclosure of legislative proposals/topics is a reporting duty imposed on principals as a condition of lobbying, not a separate lobbyist-filed spending report requirement.

Compensation to lobbyists is reported by the principal in its expense statement, while the lobbyist only supplies information to the principal and is not required to file a compensation disclosure report as the named filer.
The required time record is filed by the principal and does not mandate a lobbyist-filed contact disclosure report.
Issue/time allocation (10%+ topics) is reported by the principal in its expense statement and there is no lobbyist-filed expenditure-per-issue report.
Reporting of topics/legislative proposals for lobbying communications is required of principals, not of lobbyists via a separate spending report.
The statute’s lobbying-activity identification (topics, proposals, rule numbers) is a principal reporting requirement and does not create a lobbyist-filed activity/spending report.
Although principals report lobbying expenditures, Wisconsin does not require lobbyists to file their own disclosure report covering gifts/entertainment/transportation/lodging.
Indirect lobbying costs (non-compensation) are elements of the principal’s expense statement, with lobbyists only providing information, not filing a separate report.
Because the statute requires principals—not lobbyists—to file periodic expense statements, lobbyists are not required to file itemized spending reports including issues/bills and compensation.
A lobbyist’s license application may include a residence address, but the statute does not require lobbyists to disclose address/phone in a separate periodic spending report.

Identification of legislative proposals/rule numbers/topics is required to be reported by principals, so lobbyists are not required to reveal targeted legislation/executive actions in a separate spending report.
The nature/purpose of the principal’s business/interest is disclosed in the principal’s registration statement, not through a lobbyist-filed spending report.
Principal name and business address are disclosed by the principal in its registration; lobbyists are not required to disclose principals’ address/phone in a separate spending report.

Authorizations to represent principals are filed (by the lobbyist or principal) before lobbying, but the statute does not require lobbyists to file a periodic spending report listing all principals represented.
Bill/proposal/rule-number reporting is imposed on principals (and as a condition of authorizing lobbying), not on lobbyists via a separate spending report.
Direct lobbying costs including compensation to lobbyists are reported in the principal’s expense statement and lobbyists do not file a separate spending report as named filers.
Total lobbying expenditures are required to be reported by registered principals, not by lobbyists in a separate periodic spending report.
The statutory scheme requires principals to file expense statements and only requires lobbyists to provide supporting information, so there is no lobbyist-filed itemized spending/compensation report.
The statute mandates principal expense statements each period but does not require a lobbyist to file a separate ‘no activity’ spending report.

The only itemized recipient reporting concerns reimbursements authorized under § 13.621(7)(a) to specified officials/candidates, and there is no lobbyist-filed report requiring disclosure of spending on household members of public officials.
While principals must file certain detailed components, lobbyists are not the required filers of any itemized spending report under the statute.
